prov_lac_ha.name: Lạc Hà
prov_lac_ha.lore: A low swell of steppe and grass along the river, crowned by the ochre terraces and rose-tiled halls of Lạc Hà Tông. Its people serve the sect as farmers, boatmen and servants, and every evening the whole land turns to watch the sun go down through the Sunset Ring. An Earth vein under the steppe near the seat is said to be strongest in the hour of the evening glow.

prov_nam_pho.name: Nam Phố
prov_nam_pho.lore: Old forest on the river mouth shore around the cloud-painted hall of Nam Phố Đường. Its people are scribes, paper makers and ink grinders. Golden pheasants nest in the meadow by the hall, and the scribes buy their tail feathers for fine brushes.

prov_p136.name: Hoa Khê
prov_p136.lore: Forest and grass along the flower brook, with a little bamboo. Its cottages keep the custom of the lovers' slips and pay their dues to Nam Phố Đường. Wild plum trees line the river and fill it with petals in spring.

prov_p137.name: Ngân Than
prov_p137.lore: Forest and grass on a gravel river bend, rising to wooded hills. Its panners wash the shallows for the silver of Lạc Hà's coin. The wind in the forest on the hills sounds like flutes, and the panners say it keeps the count.

prov_p138.name: Phương Thảo
prov_p138.lore: Forest and sea meadow behind low dunes at a river mouth. Its people cut the sweet grass for the mats of Lạc Hà's meditation halls. A wood of sea pines shelters the meadow from the salt wind.

prov_p139.name: Thủy Khẩu
prov_p139.lore: Grass, forest and steppe where the brook joins the river at the hand-dug channel. Its people live by the boat trade and lift a spadeful each winter so the river will remember. A sweet hot spring rises in the grass nearby.

prov_p51.name: Hạc Đinh
prov_p51.lore: Steppe and grass where the river spreads into shallows below the sect, around the islet market of Hạc Đinh Thị. Its people trade pills, river fish and talismans among the cranes. An Earth vein lies under a long sandy isle in the shallows.

prov_p79.name: Phong Lâm
prov_p79.lore: Red maple forest where the river meets the sea, round the harbour town kept by Nam Phố Đường. Its people are clerks, timber hands and fishers, and the swallows nest on the Tạ clan hall. Great owls live in the maples and are left alone, since they keep the town's granaries clear of rats.

prov_p80.name: Tang Ma
prov_p80.lore: Forest and grass along the river, planted with mulberry and blue-flowering hemp around Tang Ma Thành. Its people weave silk and twist the ropes the ferrymen trust. A wild mulberry wood gives the silkworms of the poorest families their leaves.

prov_r13_1.name: Thạch Trụ Lâm
prov_r13_1.lore: A coast of grey karst pillars and forest, honeycombed with caves where beasts den. No one lives here; Lạc Hà holds the Jade Milk Spring but sends its disciples only in groups. Lime-cutters come for the cave stone and leave before dark.

prov_r13_10.name: Than Đầu
prov_r13_10.lore: Steppe, forest, grass and red badlands climbing from a river to high bare ground. Its villagers fish the rapids and ferry goods past them. A Metal vein on the high badlands draws Lạc Hà's sword disciples.

prov_r13_11.name: Sùng A Lĩnh
prov_r13_11.lore: Forest, high mountains, steppe and badlands, the highest ground in Ngư Ca Xuyên. No one lives here; its slopes are too steep to farm and the mountain apes drive off hunters. Lạc Hà's disciples climb it to look out over the whole river land.

prov_r13_12.name: Lô Địch
prov_r13_12.lore: Wide steppe and grass along the river below Lạc Hà's seat. Its villagers fish and play reed flutes at dusk, answering the songs of the boats. On the steppe stand the herb terraces of Yên Quang Các, which picks its herbs in the evening glow.

prov_r13_13.name: Mộ Tử Nguyên
prov_r13_13.lore: Badlands and dry steppe whose hills turn purple at dusk, as the old line says the evening hills do. No one lives here; there is no water. An Earth vein in the badlands draws Lạc Hà's disciples to cultivate at sunset.

prov_r13_14.name: Hồng Nham Hoang
prov_r13_14.lore: High red badlands and bare mountains with no water and no road. No one lives here but copper miners in summer. A boiling spring among the crags is the only water for a day's walk.

prov_r13_2.name: Vạn Động Lĩnh
prov_r13_2.lore: Forest and karst full of caves and winding gorges. No one lives here; the caves are dens and the gorges flood. Gypsum cutters come in the dry season for the white stone the alchemists use.

prov_r13_3.name: Hầu Đầu
prov_r13_3.lore: Forest and karst on high ground with no river. Its villagers grow wood-ear mushrooms on cut logs and gather herbs. Wild spirit boars root through the forest and break the mushroom racks.

prov_r13_4.name: Hôi Diêu
prov_r13_4.lore: Forest and karst with a little bamboo. Its villagers burn the karst stone into lime for the plaster of Lạc Hà's halls. Beside the village lies Hãm Thạch Trấn, a town that sank into the ground.

prov_r13_5.name: Phóng Mộc
prov_r13_5.lore: Forest and bamboo on a river that runs out of the hills. Its villagers fell timber and float it down to the towns of the plain. The forest on the hills above is old and layered green.

prov_r13_6.name: Sơn Trà
prov_r13_6.lore: Forest and high ground on a mountain river. Its villagers grow camellias for their oil and their tea. Grey wolves hunt the high forest and come down in hard winters.

prov_r13_7.name: Vãn Đăng
prov_r13_7.lore: Grass and forest on the coast. Its fishers put out lamps on their boats at dusk and sing as they come home. A Water vein lies inland where the clouds break after rain.

prov_r13_8.name: Lăng Hoa
prov_r13_8.lore: Grass, forest and steppe along the river. Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the river ponds. A Wood vein runs under the maples on the higher ground.

prov_r13_9.name: Vân Gian
prov_r13_9.lore: Forest, grass and high mountains on the uplands. Its villagers gather herbs and chestnuts in the mountain forest. Above them stand the ruins of Vân Kiều Trấn, a mining town that emptied when its silver ran out.

prov_lac_ha_spirit_vein_1.name: Tề Phi Mạch
prov_lac_ha_spirit_vein_1.look: A low rise of steppe below the seat where, at dusk, the sunset clouds and the wild ducks seem to fly together overhead.
prov_lac_ha_spirit_vein_1.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, named for the line in which the sunset clouds fly with the lone wild duck. Lạc Hà's inner disciples cultivate here at evening, and it is strongest in the hour of the glow.

prov_nam_pho_beast_lair_1.name: Cẩm Kê Nguyên
prov_nam_pho_beast_lair_1.look: A grassy meadow by the hall where red and gold pheasants strut among the paper-drying lines.
prov_nam_pho_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit golden pheasants nest here, and their spurs can open a man's leg. The scribes of Nam Phố Đường buy their moulted tail feathers for fine brushes and leave the birds alone.

prov_p136_forest_1.name: Lạc Mai Lâm
prov_p136_forest_1.look: A wood of wild plums along the river that turns white with blossom before the snow is gone.
prov_p136_forest_1.lore: Its petals float down to the flower brook each spring and catch on the lovers' fence. The village's old women say a slip that catches in the plum petals is the luckiest of all.

prov_p137_forest_1.name: Sảng Lại Lâm
prov_p137_forest_1.look: A forest on the hills where the wind through the hollow branches sounds like many flutes.
prov_p137_forest_1.lore: Its name comes from the old line about clear pipes sounding and a clean wind rising. The silver panners of Ngân Than say the forest keeps the count when their singers tire.

prov_p138_forest_1.name: Yển Tùng Lâm
prov_p138_forest_1.look: A wood of low, wind-bent pines behind the dunes, their crowns all leaning away from the sea.
prov_p138_forest_1.lore: The sea pines shelter the sweet grass meadow from the salt wind. The grass cutters of Phương Thảo say that the day the pines fall the grass will lose its scent.

prov_p139_hot_spring_1.name: Cam Lộ Tuyền
prov_p139_hot_spring_1.look: A warm spring in the grass above the river, its water sweet enough to drink.
prov_p139_hot_spring_1.lore: The boatmen of Thủy Khẩu fill their jars here before going downriver. Lạc Hà's cooks send for it to brew the tea of the evening rites.

prov_p51_spirit_vein_1.name: Trường Châu Mạch
prov_p51_spirit_vein_1.look: A long sandy isle in the shallows above the market, its steppe grass thick and green.
prov_p51_spirit_vein_1.lore: An Earth vein lies under the isle, named for the old line about the long isle of the prince. The cranes of Hạc Đinh roost here at night, and the sect's disciples wade out to cultivate among them.

prov_p79_beast_lair_1.name: Phong Kiêu Lâm
prov_p79_beast_lair_1.look: A dark stand of old maples above the town where pellets and bones lie thick under the branches.
prov_p79_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit owls as large as a child roost here and hunt the river land by night. They take rats from the granaries and the occasional lamb, and the townsfolk count the bargain fair.

prov_p80_forest_1.name: Dã Tang Lâm
prov_p80_forest_1.look: A tangled wood of wild mulberries on the river, purple with fallen fruit in summer.
prov_p80_forest_1.lore: The poorest families of Tang Ma pick leaves here for their silkworms. Children come in summer to paint their door charms in the purple juice.

prov_r13_1_mine_1.name: Chung Nhũ Quật
prov_r13_1_mine_1.look: A deep cave among the karst pillars whose roof hangs with milky stone icicles, many of them cut short.
prov_r13_1_mine_1.lore: Cutters take the stalactite stone here for the alchemists, who grind it into pills for the lungs. They work in groups and leave before dark, for other caves in the pillars are dens.

prov_r13_10_village_1.name: Than Đầu Thôn
prov_r13_10_village_1.look: A steppe village by a stretch of rocky river rapids, with a hauling path cut along the bank.
prov_r13_10_village_1.lore: Its villagers fish the rapids and haul the boats past them on ropes for a toll. The boatmen sing as they haul, and the songs are older than the village.

prov_r13_10_spirit_vein_2.name: Thiết Cốt Mạch
prov_r13_10_spirit_vein_2.look: A ridge of dark badland rock where seams of grey metal stand out like bones.
prov_r13_10_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Metal vein runs under the ridge, hard and cold. Lạc Hà's sword disciples cultivate here to temper their bodies before taking up a blade.

prov_r13_11_beast_lair_1.name: Sơn Tiêu Nhai
prov_r13_11_beast_lair_1.look: A high cliff of bare rock where red-faced apes sit on the ledges and hurl stones at anyone below.
prov_r13_11_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit mountain apes live on the cliff and drive off hunters and climbers. They are said to remember a face and stone that person for years.

prov_r13_12_village_1.name: Lô Địch Thôn
prov_r13_12_village_1.look: A river village of reed-thatched houses where reed flutes hang drying from the eaves.
prov_r13_12_village_1.lore: Its fishers play reed flutes at dusk, answering the songs of the boats on the river. In 803 the flutes fell silent with the boats, and the village still plays one tune less on that dusk.

prov_r13_12_hot_spring_2.name: Hà Quang Tuyền
prov_r13_12_hot_spring_2.look: A hot spring on a steppe rise whose steam glows rose-red at sunset.
prov_r13_12_hot_spring_2.lore: Lạc Hà's disciples bathe here after cultivating at dusk. The herbalists of Yên Quang Các water their evening herbs from it.

prov_r13_12_minor_seat_p.name: Yên Quang Các
prov_r13_12_minor_seat_p.look: A pavilion of ochre walls on the steppe, surrounded by terraced herb beds that its disciples tend only at sunset.
prov_r13_12_minor_seat_p.lore: Alchemists sworn to Lạc Hà Tông founded the pavilion in 1065, after the old line about the haze and light congealing as the evening hills turn purple. They pick their herbs only in the hour of the evening glow and say the herbs hold the light. Lạc Hà's disciples buy most of its pills.

sect.name: Yên Quang Các
sect.craft: alchemy (luyện đan) from steppe herbs picked at dusk

prov_r13_13_spirit_vein_1.name: Ngưng Tử Mạch
prov_r13_13_spirit_vein_1.look: A hollow among badland hills where the dusk light pools in a deep purple long after sunset.
prov_r13_13_spirit_vein_1.lore: An Earth vein runs under the hollow, and it holds the purple of the evening hills longest. Lạc Hà's disciples cultivate here in the last light.

prov_r13_14_hot_spring_1.name: Phí Thạch Tuyền
prov_r13_14_hot_spring_1.look: A boiling spring among red crags, its water bubbling up through stones too hot to touch.
prov_r13_14_hot_spring_1.lore: It is the only water for a day's walk in the waste. Copper miners cool its water in jars overnight before they drink.

prov_r13_14_mine_2.name: Tử Đồng Khoáng
prov_r13_14_mine_2.look: Shallow pits in the red badlands, half filled with sand, beside old heaps of green-stained rock.
prov_r13_14_mine_2.lore: Lạc Hà once dug its coin and bell copper here, but the shallow ore is nearly spent. A few miners still pick over the heaps in summer; in winter the pits are left to the wind.

prov_r13_2_gorge_1.name: Oanh Hồi Hạp
prov_r13_2_gorge_1.look: A narrow karst gorge that winds back and forth between grey walls, so that a walker sees the same pillar three times.
prov_r13_2_gorge_1.lore: Its name comes from the old line about islands and isles winding round. The gorge floods in the rains, and gypsum cutters cross it only in the dry season.

prov_r13_2_mine_2.name: Bạch Cao Động
prov_r13_2_mine_2.look: A cave in the karst whose walls are crusted with soft white gypsum, scraped in long grooves.
prov_r13_2_mine_2.lore: Cutters scrape gypsum here for the alchemists, who use it in cooling pills, and for the plaster of fine halls. The cave is cold even in summer.

prov_r13_3_village_1.name: Hầu Đầu Thôn
prov_r13_3_village_1.look: A forest village where stacks of cut logs lean in the shade, studded with dark wood-ear mushrooms.
prov_r13_3_village_1.lore: Its villagers grow wood-ear mushrooms on cut logs and gather herbs in the high forest. Their dried mushrooms go down to Hạc Đinh Thị.

prov_r13_3_beast_lair_2.name: Cuồng Trư Lâm
prov_r13_3_beast_lair_2.look: A high forest whose floor is rooted up and torn, with tusk marks on the trunks.
prov_r13_3_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit boars as heavy as an ox root here and charge anything that moves. They break the mushroom racks of Hầu Đầu, and the village hires Lạc Hà's outer disciples to drive them back each autumn.

prov_r13_4_village_1.name: Hôi Diêu Thôn
prov_r13_4_village_1.look: A forest village of white-dusted houses beside smoking lime kilns.
prov_r13_4_village_1.lore: Its villagers burn the karst stone into lime for the plaster of Lạc Hà's halls. Everything in the village is white, and its children are called the ghosts of Ngư Ca.

prov_r13_4_gorge_2.name: U Lan Cốc
prov_r13_4_gorge_2.look: A narrow karst valley where wild orchids grow on the damp walls.
prov_r13_4_gorge_2.lore: The orchids grow only in its shade, and herbalists climb its walls for them. The lime-burners leave its stone alone.

prov_r13_4_ruin_3.name: Hãm Thạch Trấn
prov_r13_4_ruin_3.look: A ring of broken walls in the forest around a deep round pit where the town's centre used to be.
prov_r13_4_ruin_3.lore: Lime-burners built the town in 340 on the edge of the karst. In 912 the ground under its market fell into a cave, and the rest of the town was left within a year. Its people moved to Hôi Diêu and have never built on bare karst since.

prov_r13_5_village_1.name: Phóng Mộc Thôn
prov_r13_5_village_1.look: A river village where cut logs are rolled into the water and floated off in long chains.
prov_r13_5_village_1.lore: Its villagers fell timber in the hills and float it down to the plain. Each log is branded with the family's mark, and the downriver towns pay by the mark.

prov_r13_5_forest_2.name: Tằng Thúy Lâm
prov_r13_5_forest_2.look: An old forest on the hills, its layers of green rising one above the other like stacked ranges.
prov_r13_5_forest_2.lore: Its name comes from the old line about layered ranges rising green. The timber cutters of Phóng Mộc take only the trees at its edge.

prov_r13_6_village_1.name: Sơn Trà Thôn
prov_r13_6_village_1.look: A mountain village on a river where camellia bushes line every terrace.
prov_r13_6_village_1.lore: Its villagers grow camellias for their oil and their tea. The oil goes to the lamps of Lạc Hà's halls.

prov_r13_6_beast_lair_2.name: Quần Lang Lĩnh
prov_r13_6_beast_lair_2.look: A high forested ridge where wolf trails run under the trees and howls carry at night.
prov_r13_6_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit grey wolves hunt the ridge in packs. In hard winters they come down to the camellia terraces, and the villagers light fires all night.

prov_r13_7_village_1.name: Vãn Đăng Thôn
prov_r13_7_village_1.look: A forest village on the coast where every boat hangs a lamp at the stern.
prov_r13_7_village_1.lore: Its fishers put out at dusk with lamps and come home singing. On the dusk of the mourning for 803 they light the lamps but do not put out.

prov_r13_7_spirit_vein_2.name: Vân Tiêu Mạch
prov_r13_7_spirit_vein_2.look: A grassy hollow inland where the clouds break first after rain and the light pours through.
prov_r13_7_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Water vein runs under the hollow, named for the old line about clouds melting and rain clearing. The fishers of Vãn Đăng say the weather turns here first.

prov_r13_8_village_1.name: Lăng Hoa Thôn
prov_r13_8_village_1.look: A river village of grassy banks and ponds covered with the floating leaves of water chestnuts.
prov_r13_8_village_1.lore: Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the river ponds and gather them from small round tubs. Girls who can paddle a tub without spilling are thought to make good wives.

prov_r13_8_spirit_vein_2.name: Phong Ảnh Mạch
prov_r13_8_spirit_vein_2.look: A grove of red maples on the higher ground whose shadows lie unusually sharp and still.
prov_r13_8_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein runs under the maples. Lạc Hà's disciples say it is a cutting from the maples of the founder's first hall.

prov_r13_9_village_1.name: Vân Gian Thôn
prov_r13_9_village_1.look: A mountain village in the forest, often wrapped in cloud, with chestnut trees around its houses.
prov_r13_9_village_1.lore: Its villagers gather herbs and chestnuts in the mountain forest. They are descended from the miners of Vân Kiều Trấn and still keep their picks over the door.

prov_r13_9_spirit_vein_2.name: Cổ Bách Mạch
prov_r13_9_spirit_vein_2.look: A high slope of ancient cypresses whose trunks are twisted like rope.
prov_r13_9_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood vein runs under the cypresses, the oldest trees in Ngư Ca Xuyên. Lạc Hà's elders go there to cultivate in solitude.

prov_r13_9_ruin_3.name: Vân Kiều Trấn
prov_r13_9_ruin_3.look: Ruined stone houses on a high mountain shoulder, reached by a broken stone bridge over a gorge.
prov_r13_9_ruin_3.lore: Silver miners built the town in 520 under Lạc Hà Tông, and reached it by a stone bridge often lost in cloud. By 1040 its silver was gone and its people had moved down to Vân Gian. The bridge broke in a storm a few years later.
